messages.body_plain:
Hi Nada,

your problem is not reproducible for me because of the datasets referenced, but a similar example (see below) for me is working
Could the problem be related to your datasets?

ui <- fluidPage(
        tabPanel("Downloading Data",
          titlePanel("Download Data"),
          sidebarLayout(
            sidebarPanel(

              selectInput("dataset",label="Choose a dataset:",c("iris","mtcars")),

              downloadButton("downloadData","Download")
            ),
            mainPanel(
              tableOutput("tab3")
            )
          )
        )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  datasetInput<-reactive({

    switch(input$dataset,"iris"=iris,"mtcars"=mtcars)

  })
  output$tab3<-renderTable({
    datasetInput()
  })
  output$downloadData<-downloadHandler(
    filename=function(){
      paste(input$dataset,".csv",sep="")
    },
    content=function(file){
      write.csv(datasetInput(),file,row.names = FALSE)
    })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

Luca,

Thanks for the insight, but as I said, I’m very new to all this and creating a reactive function is something I’ll need to research more.  And thanks for pointing me to the update* functions - I didn't know that was possible.

Here is a highly minimized concept of what I’m trying to achieve.  A loop, within the server that can update the display in the shiny dashboard:

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(

    # Application title
    titlePanel("My Test"),

    # Start Sim
    actionButton(inputId = "start",
                label = "Start"),

    # Display status
    mainPanel(
          htmlOutput("f0")
    )
)

# Define server logic
server <- function(input, output, session) {

    observeEvent(input$start, {

        for (i in 1:10) {

            output$f0 <- renderText({
                paste("Number: ", runif(1,1,10))
            })

            invalidateLater(1000, session)

        }
    })
}

# Run the application
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

Mikey
